c.tagline: UNESCO medina, Roman mosaics, and Boujaffar's endless sand.

taxi.fareNote: Yellow city taxis are cheap and metered — ask for the meter (compteur). For trips between towns, shared louages (white minibuses with a coloured stripe) leave from the louage station when full and are the standard local way to reach Monastir, Kairouan, or Tunis.

emergency.note: 197 reaches the police (Sûreté), 190 the national ambulance (SAMU), and 198 civil protection and fire.

avoid.reason: Beach resort — site of a 2015 attack; remain vigilant at tourist sites

hood_desc: The walled 9th-century old town — a UNESCO World Heritage site — wrapped around the Ribat fortress, the Great Mosque, the kasbah with its mosaic-filled archaeological museum, and a warren of souks; best for first-timers who want the city's history and character on their doorstep.

The downtown grid just outside the medina walls around Avenue Habib Bourguiba and Place Farhat Hached, with the train station, banks, cafes, and everyday shops; a convenient, well-connected central base close to both the old town and the seafront.

The long Boujaffar beachfront and its palm-lined corniche promenade, packed with sunbathers by day and strolling families and cafes by night; a relaxed seaside base right on the sand in the middle of the city.

A residential and resort strip north of the centre along the coast toward Kantaoui, lined with mid-range and family beach hotels and quieter than downtown; suits travelers who want the beach with a calmer pace.

A purpose-built marina resort about 10 km north of Sousse, ringed with whitewashed Andalusian-style villas, yacht berths, golf, restaurants, and bars; the liveliest spot for dining and going out after dark.

water.note: Tap water is chlorinated but most visitors and many locals drink bottled.

transit.hours: Sahel Metro trains run roughly 5:00 AM to 10:00 PM; SORETRAS city buses run from early morning until about 9:00 PM.
transit.note: Sousse is the northern terminus of the Sahel Metro (Métro du Sahel), an above-ground light-rail line linking Sousse with Monastir and Mahdia down the coast. In-town SORETRAS city buses cover the rest, and yellow taxis and shared louages fill the gaps.
transit.pay: Sahel Metro and bus tickets are bought in cash at station windows or on board; there is no rechargeable smart card and fares are only a dinar or two.

bus: SNTRI intercity coaches to Tunis and other cities
Louages (shared taxis) to Monastir, Kairouan, and Tunis
train: SNCFT mainline trains to Tunis and Sfax

transit.m: Airport shuttle or transfer to Sousse (~40-50 min)
Taxi to Sousse city center (40-50 min)

tip.r: Service isn't included; rounding up or leaving about 5-10% at restaurants and cafes for good service is appreciated but not expected.
